abstract: Recent measurements of Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO) from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Survey (DESI DR2), combined with data from the cosmic microwave background (CMB) and Type Ia supernovae (SNe), challenge the <math altimg="si109.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3213"><mi>Λ</mi></math>-Cold Dark Matter (<math altimg="si109.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3219"><mi>Λ</mi></math>CDM) paradigm. They indicate a potential evolution in the dark energy equation of state (EoS), <math altimg="si113.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3224"><mrow><mi>w</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>, as suggested by analyses that employ parametric models. In this paper, we use a model-independent approach known as high performance symbolic regression (PySR) to reconstruct <math altimg="si113.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3238"><mrow><mi>w</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> directly from observational data, allowing us to bypass prior assumptions about the underlying cosmological model. Our findings confirm that the DESI DR2 data alone agree with the <math altimg="si109.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3251"><mi>Λ</mi></math>CDM model (<math altimg="si6.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3257"><mrow><mi>w</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>) at the redshift range considered. Additionally, when combining DESI data with existing compilations of SN distance measurements, such as Patheon+ and DESY5, we observe no deviation from the <math altimg="si109.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3276"><mi>Λ</mi></math>CDM model within <math altimg="si195.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3282"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>σ</mi></mrow></math> (C.L.) for the interval of values of present-day matter density parameter <math altimg="si309.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3290"><msub><mrow><mi>Ω</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub></math> and the sound horizon at the drag epoch <math altimg="si310.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3300"><msub><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub></math> currently constrained by observational data. Therefore, similarly to the DESI DR1 case, these results suggest that it is still premature to claim statistically significant evidence for a dynamical EoS or deviations from the <math altimg="si109.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3310"><mi>Λ</mi></math>CDM model based on the current DESI data in combination with supernova measurements.
title: Evidence for dynamical dark energy from DESI-DR2 and SN data? A symbolic regression analysis
